text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — APAC GPU onboarding is failing at the keystore decrypt step and we're seeing SIEM writes get 403'd. Blocks new nodes from joining warm pools.
Meera Patel: :eyes: seeing same, got an alert from infra-bot about 401/403 to https://siem.redwood.internal from keystore-proxy.
Samir Kapoor: Stacktrace in node logs shows `kms:Decrypt` failing with `AccessDenied`. But the keystore healthcheck still returns 200.
Maria Gomez: I pulled a failed node: /var/log/redwood/keystore.log shows repeated TLS 403 on POST /ingest/audit.
Alex Chen: Important detail — this started after yesterday's egress ACL tighten in apac-core-nets (NACL rule 102 applied). Could be NACL + firewall interplay.
Meera Patel: We rolled a conditional IAM policy for ephemeral keystore role around 03:12 UTC to restrict external write destinations. Might be too strict for the SIEM IP range.
Samir Kapoor: Repro steps: `curl -v https://keystore-proxy.apac.internal/health` -> OK. `curl -v -X POST https://siem.redwood.internal/ingest -H \"Authorization: Bearer ...\"` -> 403 from SIEM (rejects IP or IAM).
Maria Gomez: SIEM team says they saw requests but rejected due to missing client cert SAN match (they tightened mTLS last week). Could be the same window.
Alex Chen: So hypothesis: (1) NACL denies ephemeral egress so client cert handshake fallsback -> SIEM rejects. (2) IAM conditional removed ephemeral role's `kms:Decrypt` target due to principal ARN mismatch. Both cause provisioning failure.
Meera Patel: Quick mitigation proposal: open temporary egress allowlist for SIEM CIDR and add a canary IAM statement restoring `kms:Decrypt` to keystore-ephemeral role for apac region. Then watch for node join success.
Samir Kapoor: +1. Also suggest rate-limiting the allowlist so we don't blast SIEM during backlog. We should add a short TTL (30m) on the NACL change.
Maria Gomez: I'll coordinate with SIEM to accept connections from the allowlist and confirm mTLS SAN mapping.
oncall-rotations: infra-bot noticed 23 nodes in warm-pool stuck at "decrypted=false". Current queue length: 12k onboarding jobs.
Alex Chen: Cost tradeoff: letting the queue drain means GPU billing while nodes idle. If we do a staged unblock (canary 2 nodes) we limit cost while verifying SIEM acceptance.
Meera Patel: I'll apply the NACL change to just the canary subnet (apac-warm-1) + grant the IAM change scoped to ec2:instanceProfile arn:aws:iam::123456:instance-profile/keystore-ephemeral-apac-canary.
Samir Kapoor: Commands I'm running now (will paste results):
```
# list stuck nodes
kubectl -n infra get pods -l svc=warm-pool -o wide | grep Pending
# check keystore errors
kubectl -n infra logs keystore-proxy-abc123 | tail -n 50
```
Meera Patel: Done — applied canary NACL and IAM patch. Pushing minimal `kms:Decrypt` allow for the canary instance profile.
Maria Gomez: SIEM acknowledged canary IPs and accepted the mTLS cert. Can see `200 OK` on ingest.
Alex Chen: Can confirm two nodes in apac-warm-1 transitioned to `decrypted=true` and joined warm pool. Onboarding queue dropped from 12k -> 11.2k.
Samir Kapoor: Nice. We should craft rollback plan: if SIEM rejects or we see unexpected traffic, revert NACL and revoke IAM grant. Also log the exact change IDs.
Meera Patel: Filed change CR: CHG-2026-apac-keystore-egress-temp. Rolling to 4 more subnets in staged windows (10m apart) once we validate metrics.
Maria Gomez: SIEM team requests a short-lived audit window capture for the canary traffic to verify no PII leaks — we can enable verbose audit for that profile for 1h.
Alex Chen: Good call. Also follow-up: need to reconcile why the mTLS SAN change + IAM conditional shipped without test in apac. Add to postmortem.
sec-bot: Automated check: no public keys were exposed. No policy escalations detected in the account during the change window.
oncall-rotations: Monitoring checklist: watch `keystore.decrypt.fail_rate`, `warm_pool.pending_count`, `siem.ingest.4xx_rate`. Alert if decrypt_fail > 5% for > 5m.
Samir Kapoor: After canary green, we should schedule a controlled rollback of the conditional IAM and update the playbook to include SIEM mTLS SAN mapping as a dependency for keystore policy changes.
Meera Patel: Agreed. I'll update runbook and add a prompt in the PR template: \"have you verified mTLS CA/SAN updates with downstream ingestors?\"
Alex Chen: Thanks all — I'll keep an eye on cost impact and open a billing ticket if the warm-pool idle hours exceed 2x baseline. Update this thread when you roll the next batch. :thumbsup:
